stage1.impression: A red acrylic turntable on a walnut sideboard against a salmon wall, with a red glass lamp cropped at right: tidy and warm, but it reads as a clean CG product render, not a dusk living room. The brightest thing in the frame is the blank wall. The turntable is slightly soft and darker than its background. The record is a mirror-smooth grey disc with no grooves, and the lamp is clearly not switched on, so the idea of a record player lit by its lamp at dusk never lands.

blocking_9: The record player must be the sharpest and best-separated thing in the frame: crisp edges on the platter rim and tonearm, with the wall darker than the product's highlights.
The lamp must visibly be on: a glowing shade and a warm pool of light on the walnut that lights the plinth, so the acrylic glows with transmitted light.
Dusk must read: cool blue window light on one side against the warm lamp, and the wall should be a warm cream, not a uniform salmon.
The record must read as vinyl: black, with groove sheen and a fine anisotropic highlight, not a polished grey mirror.
The loudspeaker named in the brief must appear as context, soft in the depth of the room.
No smudged plaster from the denoiser on the wall, and no high-contrast slats along the bottom edge pulling the eye out of the frame.

defects.what: The wall is the brightest area (lum median 192) and a flat orange (RGB median 248/181/134), and it upstages the product. The specified wall colour is #EEE9E1.
The plaster texture looks smudged and blotchy (denoiser), with almost no micro-detail (lum range 5 over a 60 px patch).
The record is a smooth gloss disc that mirrors the wall gradient (lum p5 to p95 is 35 to 174). There are no grooves, no run-out and no lead-in, so it reads as a grey metal disc.
The product is softer than the lamp base behind it. The focus point is about 12 cm in front of the platter, and the tonearm pillar edge is 15 px wide (10 to 90%).

The lamp is unlit: the shade is lit from outside, and there is no glow and no light pool on the cabinet (lum median under the lamp is 61, the same as the rest of the top). The lamp also competes with the hero in the same saturated red.
The plinth's lower edge is dark (lum median 23 on the platter side), so the tinted acrylic barely transmits light.
The feet read as grey plastic pucks, and their contact shadow is weak: lum 57 under the feet against 65 on the open top.
The slatted cabinet front at the bottom edge has strong contrast (lum p5 31 to p95 188) and draws the eye down and out of the frame.
The loudspeaker that is part of the brief is not in the frame.
Faint blue fringes at the acrylic edges near the arm board read as a render artefact.

changes.problem: The lamp is not on, so the shot's idea (the record player lit by its matching lamp at dusk) does not read, and the product is dark.

evidence.measured: The cabinet top under the lamp has lum median 61, the same as the rest of the top (65). The shade's lum p95 is 173 and its light is reflected, not emitted.

changes.expected: The shade glows from inside, and a warm pool falls on the walnut that reaches the motor pod and the plinth's right side. The acrylic transmits red light onto the wood.

changes.problem: The focus sits in front of the platter, so the hero is softer than the lamp behind it.

evidence.measured: The tonearm pillar edge is 15 px wide (10 to 90%) with a step of 19. camera.focus y=0.30 against the product at y=0.42.

changes.expected: The platter rim, record label, spindle and tonearm are crisp, and the lamp falls softly out of focus behind.

changes.problem: The whole frame has a heavy orange cast that turns the cream wall salmon and removes any sense of dusk.

evidence.measured: The wall's RGB median is 248/181/134 against the specified #EEE9E1. The cabinet top's blue median is 14.

changes.expected: The wall reads as warm cream, the walnut as brown rather than orange, and the red acrylic separates from the wall instead of matching it.

changes.problem: The wall is the brightest thing in the frame, while the plinth's face falls into near-black.

evidence.measured: Wall lum median 192, while the plinth's lower face measures lum median 23 at [300,700,520,760].

change.to: power_w 45, elevation 10, azimuth -35, with the target kept on the plinth so it rakes across the acrylic edge and below the wall

changes.expected: The wall drops to a mid-tone with a falloff behind the product, and the plinth edges and platter rim pick up a raking highlight and glow.

changes.problem: Dusk does not read: there is no cool light anywhere to set against the warm lamp.

evidence.measured: The left wall shows only an orange gradient (profile 197 down to 178 across x), with no cool component.

changes.expected: The left side of the wall and the record's left edge pick up a cool blue-grey tint, and the cool against warm makes the room read as dusk.

changes.problem: The record prop is a featureless gloss disc that mirrors the wall and reads as grey metal.

evidence.measured: lum p5 is 35 and p95 is 174 on what should be black vinyl, and the RGB median of 138/65/30 is the reflected wall.

change.to: vinyl: base #0A0A0B, roughness 0.18 with a concentric groove normal map (0.3 mm pitch, lead-in and run-out bands) and radial anisotropy 0.6

changes.expected: The record reads as black vinyl with a thin anisotropic highlight arc and visible track bands, and it is no longer a mirror of the wall.

changes.problem: The loudspeaker from the brief is missing, and the slatted front along the bottom edge pulls the eye out of the frame.

evidence.measured: The slats run lum p5 31 to p95 188, the highest contrast in the frame. products.0 at x=-0.6 is outside the camera's view.

change.to: [-0.05, 0.62, 0] (horn soft at left, behind the cabinet line), target [0.40, 0.42, 0.83]

changes.expected: The horn speaker reads soft at the left as context, framing the record player between speaker and lamp, and only a thin band of the cabinet front shows at the bottom.

changes.problem: The plaster is smeared by the denoiser and has no real micro-texture.

evidence.measured: lum range is 5.4 over a 60 px patch of the beige_wall_001 plaster, and the surface looks blotchy at 2x.

change.to: 768 (denoiser kept, with the albedo and normal passes as guides)

changes.expected: The plaster shows fine grain without blotches, and the acrylic edges lose their blue fringing.

out_of_scope.request: Give the feet a warmer, less plasticky finish, or hide them.
out_of_scope.why: They are part of the product. Their weight on the walnut is best addressed with the low raking key (c4) and the lamp pool (c1).

out_of_scope.request: Separate the lamp's red from the turntable's red so the lamp stops competing.
out_of_scope.why: Every piece shares one colour by design. Defocus (c2) and the lamp's own glow (c1) handle the hierarchy instead.
